latest.summary: Executive Summary Healthcare’s cyber threat landscape in 2026 extended across providers, research institutions, medical-technology companies, software ecosystems, and organizations entrusted with patient information. Ransomware remained the sector’s most visible operational threat, but credential abuse, data theft, state-sponsored espionage, destructive activity, and supply-chain compromise created additional paths to disruption and exposure. These threats frequently traveled through identities, applications, remote access services, software dependencies, vendors, and other infrastructure beyond the hospital network. This report examines those interconnected risks alongside PolySwarm telemetry on relevant ransomware families and malicious artifacts. The findings show that healthcare resilience increasingly depends on protecting trusted access, evaluating software before deployment, monitoring external dependencies, and preserving operations when technology fails. SCOPE: This report examines threats to the healthcare vertical reported from January 1 through mid-November 2026.
